outcome: Lower bounds on a(n), the longest induced path (snake) in the n-dimensional hypercube, were repeatedly improved for dimensions 9-17 during the window via heuristic/pruned search, most substantially by T. Ace (2025, dims 10-13), Orland, Fagan, Tarquini, Passaro, Manko, Heyes, Gruen, Butbaia, Tan and Gukov (arXiv:2607.15270, July 2026, dims 9-13), and Bernatonis (2026, dims 14-17); none of the sources located disclose any AI/ML method for the search itself.

disputes.summary: For dimensions 9-13, the improved bounds are attributed to at least three independent, overlapping efforts within the window: T. Ace (Zenodo, Nov 2025, dims 10-13, values 732/1439/2854 for 11/12/13), the Orland et al. arXiv paper (July 2026, dims 9-13, values 191/379/746/1476/2924 for 9-13), and the live minortriad.com records table (checked 2026-09-22, showing still-higher values 191/379/750/1480/2934 for 9-13, apparently reflecting further post-paper updates credited informally to Ace/Echols collaboration). No single source resolves current priority/attribution cleanly, and the live table already supersedes the July 2026 preprint's own numbers.

summary: The problem asks for a(n), the length of the longest induced (snake) path in the n-dimensional hypercube graph Q_n, known exactly only for n≤8. Since 26 January 2024, no resolution of the general problem occurred (it remains open for all n≥9), but the best-known lower bounds moved several times, which is squarely within scope per §3.1 since the bullet's quantity (the record length itself) is what changed. In order: T. Ace published 'New Lower Bounds for Snake-in-the-Box in 10-, 11-, 12-, and 13-dimensional Hypercubes' on Zenodo (6 November 2025, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17538015), reporting 732/1439/2854 for dimensions 11/12/13 using, per the abstract, 'simple heuristics' (a pruned breadth-first search per the companion GitHub tool docxology/snake) — no AI/ML disclosed. Then a ten-author paper from Sergei Gukov's Caltech group (Orland, Fagan, Tarquini, Passaro, Manko, Heyes, Gruen, Butbaia, Tan, Gukov), 'A Census of New Snake-in-the-Box Records' (arXiv:2607.15270, submitted 16 July 2026, revised 20 July 2026), reported new records in every dimension 9-13 (191/379/746/1476/2924), with a companion GitHub dataset (Math-AI-Caltech/Snake-in-the-Box). I read the paper's full HTML text directly (introduction, results, example, data, acknowledgements, and section list); it contains no methods/algorithm section at all describing how the authors found their snakes — it is a pure results 'census', citing predecessors' methods (genetic algorithms, evolutionary search, Monte Carlo tree search) but never stating its own. The acknowledgements credit DARPA, NSF, and a philanthropic gift, plus (per one fetch) Google Cloud TPUs and NVIDIA GPU compute grants — hardware normally used for training neural networks. This is suggestive given that several co-authors (Fagan, Tarquini, Manko, Gruen, Butbaia, Passaro, Gukov) are simultaneously authors of explicit reinforcement-learning-for-mathematics papers from the same lab in the same period (e.g. 'The Two-Hump Problem: Bridging the Difficulty Gap in Mathematical Reinforcement Learning', ICML 2026, on the Andrews-Curtis conjecture; 'RLGT: A reinforcement learning framework for extremal graph theory', on Ramsey/Turán problems) — but neither of those companion papers mentions the snake-in-the-box problem, and no source I found (paper text, GitHub READMEs for either Math-AI-Caltech/Snake-in-the-Box or Math-AI-Caltech/ACSolverX, alphaXiv digestion, Pith Review digestion) states or quotes that RL or any AI system was used for the snake search specifically. Meanwhile a separate 2026 paper by Kristijonas Bernatonis (Notre Dame) extended pruned-BFS heuristic records to dimensions 14-17 (5750/11249/21411/40835), again with no AI claimed. The live minortriad.com records table (T. Ace's own site, checked 2026-09-22) now shows even higher values for 11-13 (750/1480/2934) than the July 2026 paper, crediting continued 'sustained computational efforts of Ace and Echols' with no dates or method given in the FAQ. Wikipedia's own (non-frozen, current) Snake-in-the-box article, last touching this figure around 2026-07-23, cites minortriad.com for 191/379/746/1476/2932 and does not mention any of these researchers or any AI angle; its most recent methodologically-notable citation is a February 2023 AAAI paper (Dang, Bazgan, Cazenave, Chopin, Wuillemin, 'Warm-Starting Nested Rollout Policy Adaptation with Optimal Stopping') that did use a genuine RL-adjacent method (Nested Rollout Policy Adaptation) to improve snake-in-the-box bounds — but that result predates the window (Jan 2023) and is not counted here. Net: real, repeated, in-scope progress on the record bound (a(n) for n=9-17) occurred throughout the window, but the strongest textual evidence available describes it as heuristic/pruned search rather than AI, so ai_role is coded none under the rule that a role requires the authors' own account, which I could not find despite reading the primary paper directly and its surrounding ecosystem (GitHub, Zenodo, alphaXiv, Pith Review).
competing_reading: The TPU/GPU acknowledgement in the Orland et al. paper, combined with the fact that several of its authors are core members of an AI-for-mathematics research program (RL for Andrews-Curtis and extremal graph theory) publishing in the same months, is real circumstantial evidence that the snake search itself may have used a learned (RL or neural) heuristic/policy rather than a purely hand-coded pruning rule. If an unlocated methods appendix, supplementary material, or follow-up blog post confirms this, the correct coding would likely be ai_role 'assisted' or 'bound' (a bound moved by AI search) rather than 'none'. I was unable to access the raw PDF (binary/compressed, not parseable by my tools) and could not find a separate methods writeup, so I am not confident this circumstantial reading is wrong.
what_would_settle_it: A methods/supplementary section of arXiv:2607.15270 (or a talk, blog post, or code repository beyond the bare data-only Math-AI-Caltech/Snake-in-the-Box repo) that states in the authors' own words what search procedure produced the record snakes — specifically whether it involved a trained model (RL policy, neural network, or similar) versus a purely combinatorial/heuristic pruned search. Also, direct correspondence or a changelog on minortriad.com dating and crediting the current (750/1480/2934) records beyond the July 2026 paper's numbers.
